verdict_word: Beat and raise, with customer prepayments to fund it

headline.consensus: −$1.16 (LSEG via CNBC; CNBC noted comparability unclear)

takeaways: Revenue rose 168% to $3.661 billion, up more than $1 billion from the prior quarter, per the company release.
GAAP net loss was $709 million, or $1.27 a share, versus $110 million a year earlier; net interest expense was $846 million.
Revenue backlog was about $132.5 billion, up from about $104 billion at the end of June (company release, CNBC).
Full-year 2026 capex is now expected at $37 billion to $39 billion, raising the low end of the prior $35 billion to $39 billion range.
Q4 interest expense is guided to $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion, and exit-2026 annualized run-rate revenue guidance rose to $20 billion to $21 billion.
Management cited about $9 billion in expected customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months and said it does not plan more parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 (Investing.com).
verdict: CoreWeave sold a mountain of AI compute, raised the year, and finally answered the 'how do you pay for it' question with customer prepayments instead of another junk bond. The interest bill is still huge, but a stock down 40% in a month only needed a reason, and this was one.
